newsitem.title: GERMANY: German state Jumbo spread 15.5 bp over Bund.
newsitem.headline: German state Jumbo spread 15.5 bp over Bund.

text.p: The mandate for the German six percent, 4.5 billion-mark state Jumbo bond was awarded to a bank consortium based on a reoffer spread of 15.5 basis points over the benchmark six percent federal government bond maturing January 4, 2007, the Hesse finance ministry said on Thursday.

The consortium of banks placing the Jumbo consists of Bankgesellschaft Berlin AG, Bayerische Hypotheken- und Wechsel-Bank AG, Deutsche Girozentrale - Deutsche Kommunalbank, Helaba Landesbank Hessen-Thueringen Girozentrale, NordLB Norddeutsche Landesbank and SuedwestLB Suedwestdeutsche Landesbank, the ministry said in a statement.
The price of the bond will be fixed on Friday at about 1130 GMT. Fees amount to 32.5 pfennigs, a Helaba dealer said.
The ministry said it had had three offers from bank consortia keen to place the issue, of which two offers had met bidding requirements.
The states had stipulated that bids must be no more than 16 basis points above the yield on the benchmark federal bond.
The bond is being issued by the 10 federal states North Rhine-Westphalia, Berlin, Hamburg, Hesse, Rhineland-Palatinate, Schleswig-Holstein, Brandenburg, Bremen, Mecklenburg-Vorpommern and Saarland.
It is the second pooled state Jumbo issue of its kind. The first joint Jumbo bond was launched in August by seven states.
